newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end up on strength in properties.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end up on strength in properties.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed higher on Monday, due chiefly to positive local sentiment in the longer term outlook for the major property developers, brokers said.
"There was less selling and a more positive stance from locally based institutions," said Glenn Lesko, head of equities trading at HG Asia.
The Hang Seng Index gained 84.86 points to close at 12,626.04 after hitting a high for the day of 12,711.31 on a surprisingly strong rebound in the morning session.
Turnover rose to a respectable HK$8.06 billion, compared to Friday's HK$6.88 billion.
Volume in index stocks dropped off again on Monday, Lesko added.
Brokers said trading in China related red chips continued to dominate market activity, brokers said.
While blue chips remained on top of the turnover chart, nine of the top 20 most actively traded issues were China red chips and H shares, with only two Hong Kong-based second line issues.
The property sector led the rebound, outperforming the rest of the blue chips. Sun Hung Kai Properties led the way with a jump of HK$1.50 to HK$79.75.
Cheung Kong added HK$1.00 to HK$68.25, but Swire Pacific was one of the biggest net losers, falling HK$0.50 to HK$58.25.
H shares came under selling pressure chiefly due to the worse-than-expected results from Yizheng Chemical Fibre and Northeast Electrical Transmission.
Yizheng closed HK$0.07 lower at HK$1.32 on thin turnover of HK$13.08 million after reporting an 82 percent fall in 1996 earnings to 215.65 million yuan.
Northeast Electrical also slid HK$0.07 to HK$l.39. The company reported a 49 percent fall in 1996 earnings to 83.77 million.
The market ended on a firm note bolstered by a jump in the April Hang Seng Index future contract of 90 points to 12,625, a par with the cash market.
In the coming one to two weeks, the index should trade in a range of 12,360 to 12,900, said chartist Ted Chen of Technical Data Inc.
"The strategy for this year is to buy on dips, said Chen, who believe that the market is in an intermediate term bear market and will pull out of it the fourth quarter of the year.
